subject: Mutual action & perf readout: streaming TTFT / concurrency plan for Acme Health
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
To: Evan Torres <evan.t@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Mutual action & perf readout: streaming TTFT / concurrency plan for Acme Health

Hi Evan / Priya —

Thanks for the conversation yesterday. Per our MAP kickoff, attached is a compact performance evaluation plan focused on streaming TTFT (time-to-first-token) and end-to-end streaming latency for chat generation, plus a proposed close timeline. Key asks below so we can lock the pilot window.

Goal: provide production-grade SLAs and an acceptance artifact for your pilot by the end of the quarter. Primary success criteria: streaming TTFT (p50/p95/p99) and sustained throughput at target concurrency without >1% error rate.

Proposed evaluation matrix (see attached acme_map_v1.xlsx):
- Workloads: live-sim chat (350–800 token prompts), multi-turn context preserved (KV cache exercised)
- Metrics: TTFT p50/p95/p99, streaming p50/p95/p99 (first byte + steady-state), tokens/sec (throughput), model-side CPU/GPU utilization, error/retry rate
- Concurrency targets: 1, 4, 8, 16, 32 (ramp phases)
- Test harness: ramp-script.sh (attached) + streaming-ttft-results.csv for baseline capture
- Baseline SLOs (for acceptance): TTFT p50 < 250ms, p95 < 700ms, p99 < 1200ms at concurrency 8; throughput >= 120 tokens/sec sustained per instance; error rate <1%

Test timeline (proposed):
- Week 1 (Apr 24–28): configuration + dry run (small synthetic dataset)
- Week 2 (May 1–5): ramped concurrency tests + capture metrics
- Week 3 (May 8–12): regression checks + final acceptance report

Attachments: acme_map_v1.xlsx (MAP with owners & dates), ramp-script.sh (test harness), streaming-ttft-results.csv (format sample).

Next steps: please confirm the pilot window (prefer Apr 24 start) and whether Acme can provide a short production-like prompt corpus (anonymized) or if Redwood should supply a synthetic sample. Once agreed we’ll schedule daily 30-min standups during the test window and Marissa will own the runbook.

Thanks —
Jasmine

--
Jasmine Liu
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0191

Subject: Re: Mutual action & perf readout: streaming TTFT / concurrency plan for Acme Health

Thanks Jasmine — this looks good and aligned with what we discussed. We can confirm Apr 24 for the dry run window. A few quick clarifications:

1) We can provide an anonymized prompt corpus of ~3000 prompts that mirror production session lengths.
2) For security reasons, can the runs be done from your Dedicated region in us-west-2? We prefer not to route through eu for data residency.
3) Do you have a recommended client-side SDK version for streaming so we can instrument client-side timings?

We’ll plan to have Priya join the daily standups. Also, can you note any procurement steps we should finish before May 12 so acceptance can trigger billing?

—Evan

Subject: Re: Mutual action & perf readout: streaming TTFT / concurrency plan for Acme Health

Great — thanks for the quick confirm, Evan. A couple of operational notes from our side before Apr 24: 

- Region: us-west-2 is fine; I’ll provision a dedicated pool for the run (no cross-region routing).
- SDK: we recommend the client streaming SDK v0.9.2 (it exposes first-byte hooks). I’ll include the minimal instrumentation snippet in the runbook.
- Logging/observability: we’ll push per-request token timelines to a shared Metrics workspace and provide you a temporary read-only dashboard.

One question on acceptance SLOs: Jasmine listed TTFT p99 < 1200ms at concurrency 8. Curious if Acme would accept a stepped acceptance where p95 is the primary gate and p99 is evaluated for regression risk (i.e., p95 gate for go/no-go, p99 as risk signal). That helps keep the first-sign-off tight for billing.

Also attaching a sample CSV with the column layout we’ll publish (streaming-ttft-results.csv). Please confirm.

Thanks —
Marissa

Date: Mon, 24 Apr 2028 10:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mutual action & perf readout: streaming TTFT / concurrency plan for Acme Health

Quick update from this morning's dry run: we ran a short concurrency sweep (1, 4, 8) using the anonymized corpus. Preliminary numbers (single Redwood Dedicated pool, us-west-2):
- Concurrency 1: TTFT p50 160ms / p95 410ms / p99 760ms
- Concurrency 4: TTFT p50 175ms / p95 430ms / p99 880ms
- Concurrency 8: TTFT p50 190ms / p95 470ms / p99 920ms

Observations: latency growth is reasonably linear through 8. We captured token throughput and server-side telemetry and dropped a CSV to the shared drive (see attachment streaming-ttft-results.csv). A few errors logged when we ramped to synthetic extreme tails but overall error rate <0.7%.

Next: we’re good to run ramp to 16/32 on Tue (Apr 25) as long as Redwood is comfortable with the schedule. Also, Marissa — we agree to primary gate on p95 for initial acceptance per your suggestion. We’ll still examine p99 regressions before final sign-off.

—Evan

Subject: Re: Mutual action & perf readout: streaming TTFT / concurrency plan for Acme Health — agreed next steps

Thanks all — quick summary and next actions from Redwood's side after the ramp to 16/32 this morning: 

- Agreement: p95 primary gate; p99 health signal (no more than 5% increase vs baseline to be flagged for investigation). Acme accepted this during the standup.
- Results snapshot (post-ramp, consolidated): concurrency 16: TTFT p95 820ms, p99 1650ms (spike tail observed during a CPU throttling event); concurrency 32: TTFT p95 1270ms, p99 2800ms. We captured profiling traces and the runbook notes the exact instance ids.
- Action items for Redwood: investigate the p99 tail at 16 (likely kernel scheduling on older GPU nodes) and propose a remediation plan (kernel pinning/instance refresh). Deliverables: detailed run report (May 1) + acceptance artifact if the p95 gates hold at concurrency 8.
- Procurement/billing: Evan — per MAP we need PO/DocuSign to be completed by May 10 to align billing with acceptance windows. I’ll seed a DocuSign link in the MAP and Marissa will own the final report.

I’ll attach the profiling snapshot to the shared drive (link in the MAP). Thanks for quick coordination — we’re on track to close this pilot with a clear acceptance artifact.

—Karthik
